newsitem.title: CHINA: China state firms must prepare for WTO - academic.
newsitem.headline: China state firms must prepare for WTO - academic.

text.p: China's state-owned enterprises must prepare for an onslaught of competition from multinational companies after the country joins the World Trade Organisation (WTO), a Chinese academic said on Tuesday.

"Our country must understand the world market," said Wang Xiaoqiang, an official of the State Commission for Restructuring the Economy's economic restructuring and management research institute. "It's not a market China understands now."
China has tried for years to join the WTO and its predecessor the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade but progress has been slow due to Beijing's reluctance to allow greater market access.

More multinational companies have been challenging Chinese enterprises on their own turf following government reforms and local firms should take the opportunity to learn to compete, Wang told participants at a conference on state assets.
"Multinationals can force our enterpries to produce a wider variety of (market-oriented) products," he said.

China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Vice Minister Long Yongtu said in June that Beijing was preparing a "serious" offer on market access for the next round of WTO entry talks in Geneva, due next month.
Wang said he was not sure when China would meet success in its bid to join the WTO, but the government should back the formation of large enterpries that would be able to face competition.
China must also prepare for the opening of both its financial services and telecommunications markets -- which are now largely closed off to foreign companies -- under WTO requirements, he said.
Individual private entrepreneurs, which have flourished since the early 1980s, will be less able to face the new demands of the market after China joins the WTO, Wang said.
